```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(survey)
library(readr)

PER <- read_csv("PER.csv")
HH <- read_csv("HH.csv")

#Creating ID to combine data from household level and personal level

PER <- PER %>%
  mutate(
    hh_id = paste(
      `Schedule ID`,
      `FSU Serial No.`,
      `Sample hhld. No.`,
      sep = "_"
    ),
    person_id = paste(
      `Schedule ID`,
      `FSU Serial No.`,
      `Sample hhld. No.`,
      `Person serial no.`,
      sep = "_"
    )
  )

HH <- HH %>%
  mutate(
    hh_id = paste(
      `Schedule ID`,
      `FSU Serial No.`,
      `Sample hhld. No.`,
      sep = "_"
    )
  )


#Getting only the required columns from the PER dataset, this is done as the PER dataset is huge, therefore using only the required columns is efficient
#Keeping activity records only if start and end time is present
#Time is them converted into minutes for ease of analysis, using midnight as base, adding additional code to deal with instances where activities may cross midnight
#person_id is then created again, leading to every activity with a label telling us who performed it 

activity_data <- PER %>%
  select(
    `Schedule ID`,
    `FSU Serial No.`,
    `Sample hhld. No.`,
    `Person serial no.`,
    `day of week`,
    `time from (HH:MM)`,
    `time to (HH:MM)`,
    `3-digit activity code`
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(`time from (HH:MM)`),
    !is.na(`time to (HH:MM)`)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    start_min =
      as.numeric(`time from (HH:MM)`) / 60,

    end_min =
      as.numeric(`time to (HH:MM)`) / 60,

    end_min =
      ifelse(
        end_min <= start_min,
        end_min + 1440,
        end_min
      ),

    person_id = paste(
      `Schedule ID`,
      `FSU Serial No.`,
      `Sample hhld. No.`,
      `Person serial no.`,
      sep = "_"
    )
  )


#Finding everyone who has washing clothes as an activity at least once in their day, for these people all other activity information is also kept 
#as activities in the Time Use Survey can be done simultaneously. Example: Someone can be doing laundry from 10:00 - 11:00, while at the same time ironing previous clothes


laundry_people <- unique(
  activity_data$person_id[
    activity_data$`3-digit activity code` == 341
  ]
)

activity_data <- activity_data %>%
  filter(
    person_id %in% laundry_people
  )

cat(
  "Laundry people:",
  length(laundry_people),
  "\n"
)


#As dataset is huge, chunking is used so that the code runs more smoothly, as there are approximately 1,00,000 observations, chunks of 5,000 can be used
#Each activity is categorised into 30 minute time slots so that the number of activities happening per time slot can be counted
#Washing activities (Code 341) is kept and 30 minutes is divided equally among simultaneous activities
#Time is then added up to get total washing minutes

chunk_size <- 5000

n_chunks <- ceiling(
  length(laundry_people) / chunk_size
)

cat(
  "Chunks:",
  n_chunks,
  "\n"
)

results <- vector(
  "list",
  n_chunks
)

for (i in seq_len(n_chunks)) {

  cat(
    "Chunk",
    i,
    "of",
    n_chunks,
    "\n"
  )

  ids <- laundry_people[
    ((i - 1) * chunk_size + 1):
      min(
        i * chunk_size,
        length(laundry_people)
      )
  ]

  chunk <- activity_data %>%
    filter(
      person_id %in% ids
    ) %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(
      slot_start = list(
        seq(
          floor(start_min / 30) * 30,
          end_min - 30,
          by = 30
        )
      )
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    unnest(slot_start)

  slot_counts <- chunk %>%
    count(
      person_id,
      `day of week`,
      slot_start,
      name = "n_activities"
    )

  results[[i]] <- chunk %>%
    filter(
      `3-digit activity code` == 341
    ) %>%
    left_join(
      slot_counts,
      by = c(
        "person_id",
        "day of week",
        "slot_start"
      )
    ) %>%
    group_by(person_id) %>%
    summarise(
      laundry_minutes =
        sum(
          30 / n_activities,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}


#The chunk results are combined into one dataset
#The distribuation of calculated laundry minutes is then checked

laundry_allocated <- bind_rows(results)

summary(
  laundry_allocated$laundry_minutes
)

#One row is kept per person with relevant information
#People with no washing activity are given 0 minutes
#Household's washing type, size, expenditure etc. are added up

final_data <- PER %>%
  select(
    hh_id,
    person_id,
    `Schedule ID`,
    `FSU Serial No.`,
    `Sample hhld. No.`,
    `Person serial no.`,
    Gender,
    Age,
    Sector,
    Stratum,
    `Sub-Stratum`,
    `marital status`,
    `highest level of education`,
    `usual principal activity status (code)`,
    MULT
  ) %>%
  distinct(
    person_id,
    .keep_all = TRUE
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    laundry_allocated,
    by = "person_id"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    laundry_minutes =
      coalesce(
        laundry_minutes,
        0
      )
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    HH %>%
      select(
        hh_id,
        `Type of washing of clothes`,
        `Household size`,
        `usual monthly consumer expenditure E: [A+B+C+(D+E)/12]`
      ),
    by = "hh_id"
  )


#Now we create the variables needed for the analysis like age, gender, washing type, etc.
#There's also a variable created showing whether each person spent any time washing clothes
#People aged only 6 and above are kept for the analysis

final_data <- final_data %>%
  mutate(

    age_num =
      as.numeric(Age),

    gender_group =
      factor(
        case_when(
          Gender == 1 ~ "Male",
          Gender == 2 ~ "Female",
          Gender == 3 ~ "Transgender"
        ),
        levels =
          c(
            "Male",
            "Female",
            "Transgender"
          )
      ),

    washing_type =
      factor(
        case_when(
          `Type of washing of clothes` == 1 ~
            "Mechanical",
          `Type of washing of clothes` == 2 ~
            "Manual",
          `Type of washing of clothes` == 3 ~
            "Outsourced"
        ),
        levels =
          c(
            "Manual",
            "Mechanical",
            "Outsourced"
          )
      ),

    education_factor =
      factor(
        `highest level of education`
      ),

    marital_factor =
      factor(
        `marital status`
      ),

    principal_activity_factor =
      factor(
        `usual principal activity status (code)`
      ),

    household_size =
      as.numeric(
        `Household size`
      ),

    household_expenditure =
      as.numeric(
        `usual monthly consumer expenditure E: [A+B+C+(D+E)/12]`
      ),

    laundry_positive =
      as.numeric(
        laundry_minutes > 0
      )
  ) %>%
  filter(
    age_num >= 6
  )

#Make R account for the way that the TUS survey was designed, includings weights, cluster, strata etc
#Weights allow the study to describe wider populations

reg_design <- svydesign(
  ids =
    ~`FSU Serial No.` + hh_id,

  strata =
    ~interaction(
      Stratum,
      `Sub-Stratum`,
      drop = TRUE
    ),

  weights = ~MULT,

  data = final_data,

  nest = TRUE
)


#Calculating weighted average laundry time for each gender and washing combination
#This should output descriptive comparison between men, women and transgender respondents
#Differences between manual, mechanical and outsourced washing is also shown

gender_washing_means <- svyby(
  ~laundry_minutes,
  ~gender_group + washing_type,
  reg_design,
  svymean,
  na.rm = TRUE,
  vartype = "se"
)

print(gender_washing_means)


#The main regression is then run to examine the relation between gender and washing type
#Key variable is gender x washing type, other characteristics are controlled


model_main <- svyglm(
  laundry_minutes ~
    gender_group * washing_type +
    age_num +
    education_factor +
    marital_factor +
    principal_activity_factor +
    household_size +
    household_expenditure +
    Sector,
  design = reg_design
)

summary(model_main)


#Participation model to check whether someone washed clothes at all
#It looks at the probability of washing time rather than  number of minute spent
#It can help us figure out whether time differences are because of lack in participation

part1_model <- svyglm(
  laundry_positive ~
    gender_group * washing_type +
    age_num +
    education_factor +
    marital_factor +
    principal_activity_factor +
    household_size +
    household_expenditure +
    Sector,
  design = reg_design,
  family = quasibinomial()
)

summary(part1_model)


#Now we consider only the people who are participating in washing clothes
#This means that we can get the time of people spent washing clothes separately from those who did not participate

part2_model <- svyglm(
  laundry_minutes ~
    gender_group * washing_type +
    age_num +
    education_factor +
    marital_factor +
    principal_activity_factor +
    household_size +
    household_expenditure +
    Sector,
  design = subset(
    reg_design,
    laundry_minutes > 0
  )
)

summary(part2_model)


#The main regression is then run again and household expenditure is replaced with log expenditure


logexp_data <- final_data %>%
  mutate(
    log_expenditure =
      log(household_expenditure)
  )

logexp_design <- svydesign(
  ids =
    ~`FSU Serial No.` + hh_id,
  strata =
    ~interaction(
      Stratum,
      `Sub-Stratum`,
      drop = TRUE
    ),
  weights = ~MULT,
  data = logexp_data,
  nest = TRUE
)

model_logexp <- svyglm(
  laundry_minutes ~
    gender_group * washing_type +
    age_num +
    education_factor +
    marital_factor +
    principal_activity_factor +
    household_size +
    log_expenditure +
    Sector,
  design = logexp_design
)

summary(model_logexp)


#Transforming laundry minutes using log(1 + minutes) and running regression again, reducing influence of people with unusually high washing times and handles zero

logy_data <- final_data %>%
  mutate(
    log_laundry =
      log1p(laundry_minutes)
  )

logy_design <- svydesign(
  ids =
    ~`FSU Serial No.` + hh_id,
  strata =
    ~interaction(
      Stratum,
      `Sub-Stratum`,
      drop = TRUE
    ),
  weights = ~MULT,
  data = logy_data,
  nest = TRUE
)

model_logy <- svyglm(
  log_laundry ~
    gender_group * washing_type +
    age_num +
    education_factor +
    marital_factor +
    principal_activity_factor +
    household_size +
    household_expenditure +
    Sector,
  design = logy_design
)

summary(model_logy)


#Running main regression on only cis men and cis women as the survey unfortunately does not differentiate between trans men and trans women


mf_data <- final_data %>%
  filter(
    gender_group %in%
      c("Male", "Female")
  ) %>%
  droplevels()

mf_design <- svydesign(
  ids =
    ~`FSU Serial No.` + hh_id,
  strata =
    ~interaction(
      Stratum,
      `Sub-Stratum`,
      drop = TRUE
    ),
  weights = ~MULT,
  data = mf_data,
  nest = TRUE
)

model_mf <- svyglm(
  laundry_minutes ~
    gender_group * washing_type +
    age_num +
    education_factor +
    marital_factor +
    principal_activity_factor +
    household_size +
    household_expenditure +
    Sector,
  design = mf_design
)

summary(model_mf)


#Seeing if the relationship differs across sectors

model_sector <- svyglm(
  laundry_minutes ~
    gender_group * washing_type * Sector +
    age_num +
    education_factor +
    marital_factor +
    principal_activity_factor +
    household_size +
    household_expenditure,
  design = reg_design
)

summary(model_sector)
```

```{r}
#Final tables to be used in the report

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)


#Table 1: Weighted mean laundry time

report_table_1 <- gender_washing_means %>%
  select(
    gender_group,
    washing_type,
    laundry_minutes,
    se
  )

names(report_table_1) <- c(
  "Gender",
  "Washing type",
  "Mean laundry time (minutes)",
  "Standard error"
)

report_table_1$`Mean laundry time (minutes)` <-
  round(report_table_1$`Mean laundry time (minutes)`, 2)

report_table_1$`Standard error` <-
  round(report_table_1$`Standard error`, 2)

kable(
  report_table_1,
  caption = "Weighted Mean Time Spent Washing Clothes by Gender and Washing Type"
)


#Figure 1: Raw weighted mean laundry time

report_plot_1 <- gender_washing_means

ggplot(
  report_plot_1,
  aes(
    x = gender_group,
    y = laundry_minutes,
    fill = washing_type
  )
) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "Average Time Spent Washing Clothes",
    x = "Gender",
    y = "Average laundry time (minutes)",
    fill = "Washing type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


#Figure 2: Adjusted predicted laundry time

report_plot_2 <- data.frame(
  Gender = c(
    "Male",
    "Male",
    "Female",
    "Female"
  ),
  WashingType = c(
    "Manual",
    "Mechanical",
    "Manual",
    "Mechanical"
  ),
  PredictedTime = c(
    5.073129,
    4.589748,
    15.345432,
    13.580828
  )
)

ggplot(
  report_plot_2,
  aes(
    x = Gender,
    y = PredictedTime,
    fill = WashingType
  )
) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "Adjusted Predicted Time Spent Washing Clothes",
    x = "Gender",
    y = "Predicted laundry time (minutes)",
    fill = "Washing type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


#Table 2: Adjusted female male gap

report_table_2 <- data.frame(
  WashingType = c(
    "Manual",
    "Mechanical"
  ),
  MaleTime = c(
    5.073129,
    4.589748
  ),
  FemaleTime = c(
    15.345432,
    13.580828
  )
)

report_table_2$GenderGap <-
  report_table_2$FemaleTime -
  report_table_2$MaleTime

report_table_2$MaleTime <-
  round(report_table_2$MaleTime, 2)

report_table_2$FemaleTime <-
  round(report_table_2$FemaleTime, 2)

report_table_2$GenderGap <-
  round(report_table_2$GenderGap, 2)

names(report_table_2) <- c(
  "Washing type",
  "Male predicted time (minutes)",
  "Female predicted time (minutes)",
  "Female-male gap (minutes)"
)

kable(
  report_table_2,
  caption = "Adjusted Female-Male Gender Gap by Washing Type"
)


#Table 3, Main regression and robustness checks

report_main <- coef(summary(model_main))[
  "gender_groupFemale:washing_typeMechanical",
  c(
    "Estimate",
    "Std. Error",
    "t value",
    "Pr(>|t|)"
  )
]

report_logexp <- coef(summary(model_logexp))[
  "gender_groupFemale:washing_typeMechanical",
  c(
    "Estimate",
    "Std. Error",
    "t value",
    "Pr(>|t|)"
  )
]

report_logy <- coef(summary(model_logy))[
  "gender_groupFemale:washing_typeMechanical",
  c(
    "Estimate",
    "Std. Error",
    "t value",
    "Pr(>|t|)"
  )
]

report_mf <- coef(summary(model_mf))[
  "gender_groupFemale:washing_typeMechanical",
  c(
    "Estimate",
    "Std. Error",
    "t value",
    "Pr(>|t|)"
  )
]

report_table_3 <- rbind(
  "Main model" = report_main,
  "Log expenditure" = report_logexp,
  "Log outcome" = report_logy,
  "Male/Female only" = report_mf
)

report_table_3 <- as.data.frame(report_table_3)

report_table_3$Estimate <-
  round(report_table_3$Estimate, 3)

report_table_3$`Std. Error` <-
  round(report_table_3$`Std. Error`, 3)

report_table_3$`t value` <-
  round(report_table_3$`t value`, 3)

report_table_3$`Pr(>|t|)` <-
  signif(report_table_3$`Pr(>|t|)`, 3)

kable(
  report_table_3,
  caption = "Female × Mechanical Interaction: Main Model and Robustness Checks"
)


#Table 4: Two part model

report_participation <- coef(summary(part1_model))[
  "gender_groupFemale:washing_typeMechanical",
  c(
    "Estimate",
    "Std. Error",
    "t value",
    "Pr(>|t|)"
  )
]

report_conditional <- coef(summary(part2_model))[
  "gender_groupFemale:washing_typeMechanical",
  c(
    "Estimate",
    "Std. Error",
    "t value",
    "Pr(>|t|)"
  )
]

report_table_4 <- rbind(
  "Participation model" = report_participation,
  "Conditional time model" = report_conditional
)

report_table_4 <- as.data.frame(report_table_4)

report_table_4$Estimate <-
  round(report_table_4$Estimate, 3)

report_table_4$`Std. Error` <-
  round(report_table_4$`Std. Error`, 3)

report_table_4$`t value` <-
  round(report_table_4$`t value`, 3)

report_table_4$`Pr(>|t|)` <-
  signif(report_table_4$`Pr(>|t|)`, 3)

kable(
  report_table_4,
  caption = "Female × Mechanical Interaction in the Two-Part Model"
)
```
